As per a report by ET, this represents about 3-4% of the company’s total workforce. Flipkart confirmed the development to Inc42. While the company refrained from giving out the exact number of employees laid off post the annual review, it said that the move was a part of the regular review cycle. “Flipkart conducts regular performance reviews aligned with clearly defined expectations. As part of this process, a small percentage of employees may transition from the organisation. We are supporting affected employees with transition support,” the company said in a statement. Important to mention that terminations post annual performance reviews are typical for organisations working at the scale of Flipkart. However, typically, these layoffs impact 1-2% of a company’s workforce. For Flipkart, the trimming of the workforce comes at a time when the company is expected to file for an initial public offering (IPO) to list on the Indian bourses soon. As per a report by Moneycontrol a few days back, the company has initiated preliminary discussions with select investment bankers like Goldman Sachs, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan among others, to assess the feasibility of the public offering. “It’s too early to talk about the proposed size of the IPO and the timing of the launch, which may be by 2026 end or early 2027, but a significant part of the issue is likely to be primary in nature,” the report quotes a source as saying. Important to mention that the company has received approval from NCLT for shifting its domicile from Singapore back to India as part of preparations for the public offering. However, the total size and timeline for the IPO are yet to be determined. Alongside the workforce restructuring, Flipkart has also been streamlining its operations and assets in recent times. For instance, in the latter half of 2025, the company divested its stake from Flying Machine, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands, as well as laying off substantial holding in listed startup Shadowfax via its IPO this year. On the operations front, the ecommerce major has been doubling down on bolstering its quick commerce vertical , Flipkart Minutes. After expanding to 500 dark stores by the end of 2025, Flipkart is looking to take its dark store network count to 1,000 by the end of the first quarter of 2026. It plans to make Minutes operational in 30 Indian cities this year. Besides, the company is also said to be mulling to launch a standalone food delivery app by the end of 2026 or early next year. As per a report by ET, the Walmart-owned company is trying to zero in on a differentiated positioning in the food delivery segment. On the financial front, Flipkart Internet, the company’s marketplace arm, reported operating revenue of ₹20,493 Cr in FY25 , up 14.4% from ₹17,907 Cr in FY24.
